articles.headline: Reviewing the 2026 Season Through Finishing Averages and Stage Wins
articles.dek: A statistical look at how the championship field sorted itself out across twenty-five races.
articles.body:
Dawson Sutton captured the championship with seven hundred thirty-one points anchored by five victories. His consistency set the benchmark across the entire schedule.

Chandler Smith stayed close throughout the campaign with six hundred ninety-nine points and three wins. He capitalized on intermediate tracks and road courses alike.

Cole Butcher secured third in the final standings with six hundred seventy-six points and a single win. His ability to salvage finishes during high attrition races kept him near the front.

Kaden Honeycutt and Andrés Pérez de Lara rounded out the top five with six hundred nineteen and six hundred seventeen points respectively. Both drivers avoided major mechanical failures down the stretch to secure solid positions.

articles.headline: Spurlock Wins Homestead Finale as Sutton Secures Championship
articles.dek: Dystany Spurlock captured the victory in the final race of the season while Dawson Sutton clinched the title.
articles.body:
Dystany Spurlock drove to victory lane in the Craftsman 200 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, holding off Grant Enfinger by 0.789 seconds at the checkered flag. Spurlock started twelfth and led 52 laps during a competitive intermediate track finale that featured 8 cautions over 200 laps.

Dawson Sutton finished ninth to officially lock down the championship crown, finishing the season with 731 points and 5 victories. Chandler Smith secured second in the final standings with 699 points, while Cole Butcher claimed third with 676 points after finishing seventh in the season-ending event.

Andrés Pérez de Lara raced from a twenty-second starting position to finish third, leading 24 laps along the way. Connor Hall brought home a fourth-place result after leading 22 laps, and Connor Zilisch rounded out the top finishers in fifth with 19 laps led. Christian Eckes made the biggest move of the race, charging through the field from thirty-fifth to finish eighth. Ty Majeski suffered the only major mechanical retirement of the day, exiting the race due to an engine failure.

With the championship settled, teams now turn their attention to the offseason workshop adjustments and preparations for the upcoming year.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Bubble Watch Heading Toward Charlotte Grid Closes on Eckes
articles.dek: Bryan Dauzat holds the final transfer spot as the playoff cutoff looms over the garage.
articles.body:
The battle for the postseason grid enters its decisive phase with five events remaining before the championship reset. Ten drivers lock into the championship field following race eighteen, leaving the current cutoff line as the most watched sector of the garage. Bryan Dauzat sits tenth in the standings with 433 points, holding a narrow margin over the pursuers.

Christian Eckes finds himself on the wrong side of the cutoff in eleventh with 411 points. The gap stands at 22 markers, forcing an aggressive posture for the upcoming intermediate oval speedway date at Charlotte Motor Speedway. Kris Wright sits twelfth with 405 points, needing a reversal of recent form to bridge the deficit before the field freezes.

Further up the order, the battle for the regular season crown features Chandler Smith leading with 604 points and three victories. Dawson Sutton remains second with 577 points and four wins, keeping pressure on the top spot. Cole Butcher holds third with 559 points and one triumph, maintaining a comfortable buffer above the elimination danger zone.

Execution on pit road and stage points dictate the survival odds for the bubble contenders. Dauzat must protect his position through clean afternoon runs while Eckes searches for stage bonuses to erase the twenty-two point deficit.

articles.headline: Chandler Smith Charges From Twenty-Eighth to Win LiUNA! 150 at Lime Rock
articles.dek: Chandler Smith carved through the field from twenty-eighth on the grid to secure his third victory of the season at Lime Rock Park.
articles.body:
Chandler Smith put on a masterclass of road course racing on Saturday afternoon at Lime Rock Park, driving his thirty-eighth entry from the twenty-eighth starting spot to claim the win in the LiUNA! 150. Smith led thirty-six of the seventy laps, outdueling the rest of the field after four cautions shook up the mid-summer road course event.

Landen Lewis finished second in the forty-fifth machine after leading ten laps, crossing the finish line 1.177 seconds behind Smith. Mini Tyrell came home third, while Grant Enfinger and pole-sitter Luke Baldwin rounded out the top five. Kaden Honeycutt took sixth, followed by Layne Riggs in seventh and Kris Wright in eighth. Timmy Hill and Cole Butcher completed the top ten positions.

The afternoon proved tough on several contenders. Corey Heim exited early due to an accident, while Jake Garcia and Gio Ruggiero dropped out with transmission failures. Christopher Bell fell victim to overheating issues, and Stephen Mallozzi retired with suspension trouble.

With eleven rounds remaining before the postseason cutoff, the battle for the championship grid intensifies. Chandler Smith extends his command at the top of the standings with four hundred forty-five points and three trophies. Cole Butcher sits second with four hundred points, followed by Kaden Honeycutt and Mini Tyrell. Ty Majeski, Dawson Sutton, Frankie Muniz, and Grant Enfinger hold down the remaining provisional playoff slots as the schedule moves past the halfway mark.

The Craftsman touring division travels next to continue the regular season grind, with teams looking to secure crucial points before the playoff field locks.

articles.headline: Grant Enfinger Wins Bully Hill Vineyards 176 at Watkins Glen
articles.dek: Grant Enfinger navigated five cautions to take the victory on the road course.
articles.body:
Grant Enfinger drove to victory in the Bully Hill Vineyards 176 at Watkins Glen International, securing his first win of the sim season. Enfinger started fourth and led 18 laps during the 70-lap event, holding off hard-charging competition through a series of late restarts on the road course.

Connor Hall turned in the biggest move of the race, carving his way through the field from a 29th-place start to finish second in the #4 entry. Hall led 9 laps along the way. Mini Tyrell came home third after starting sixth and pacing the field for 8 laps, while Brandon Jones grabbed fourth. Timmy Hill rounded out the top five after starting on the pole and leading 8 laps in the #56 machine.

Five cautions slowed the race, creating heavy traffic and shake-ups throughout the 34-car field. Toni Breidinger exited due to damage vehicle policy issues, and Christopher Bell fell out following an accident. Margin of victory at the checkered flag was 0.496 seconds.

Chandler Smith continues to lead the championship standings with 252 points and one win, followed by Dawson Sutton with 219 points. Ty Majeski sits third at 218 points, with Mini Tyrell fourth at 211 points and two wins. Enfinger's win moves him to fifth in the standings with 209 points.

The series heads to the next round on the 25-race calendar as drivers continue their midseason push.

Points leader Chandler Smith holds the top spot in the championship with one hundred seventy-three points, backed by eight percent model win odds heading into Bristol. articles.headline: Mini Tyrell Charges Through Chaos to Win St. Petersburg Road Course
articles.dek: Mini Tyrell navigated five cautions and drove from twenty-fifth on the grid to capture the victory in the OnlyBulls Green Flag 150.
articles.body:
Mini Tyrell scored his second victory of the season by winning the OnlyBulls Green Flag 150 at the Streets of St. Petersburg road course. Tyrell started twenty-fifth on the thirty-four car grid and methodically worked his way to the front, leading twenty-six laps along the way. Ty Majeski chased him across the finish line, taking second place 1.542 seconds behind the winner.

The seventy-lap event on the Grand Prix circuit featured five cautions that disrupted rhythm and shook up the running order throughout the afternoon. Attrition heavily impacted the field as Justin Haley, Toni Breidinger, Layne Riggs, and Jake Garcia failed to finish due to suspensions or accidents.

Dawson Sutton drove a steady race from the twenty-third starting spot to finish third, leading eight laps. Cole Butcher followed in fourth after starting twenty-eighth and pacing the field for seven circuits. Part-time competitor Landen Lewis rounded out the top five, charging from thirteenth on the grid and leading five laps in his entry.

Chandler Smith maintained his grip on the top spot of the standings with 119 points after finishing sixth. Dawson Sutton holds second place with 96 points, while Cole Butcher sits third with 87 points. Mini Tyrell climbed to fourth with 74 points following his win, and Bryan Dauzat rounds out the top five with 70 points.

The series moves forward to the next round of the twenty-five race schedule as teams pack up and leave the Florida street circuit.

articles.headline: Early Season Surge Puts Rookie Pack on Notice at Atlanta
articles.dek: A grueling afternoon on the EchoPark superspeedway brought early answers about which new faces can run up front.
articles.body:
Two races into the schedule, the initial sorting of the field reveals clear separation among the fresh arrivals. Saturday's Fr8 208 at Atlanta Motor Speedway featured 13 yellow flags, chewing up equipment and thinning the lead pack. Through the chaos, several young competitors established themselves as weekly threats rather than simple field fillers.

Connor Zilisch delivered the most eye-catching performance of the afternoon. Starting 26th in the 35-car grid, the part-time entry carved through traffic, led 20 laps, and secured a runner-up finish 1.483 seconds behind the winner. That charge from the back stands as the biggest forward movement of the event, validating speed that showed up earlier in testing.

Dawson Sutton also continues to quietly build momentum. The sophomore driver kept his nose clean during the numerous restarts, capturing fourth place after leading 18 circuits. That consistent execution slots him second in the current standings with 62 points, trailing only Chandler Smith.

Further down the order, drivers like Andrés Pérez de Lara showed racecraft by avoiding the carnage entirely. Pérez de Lara kept his truck clean to cross eighth without leading a lap, translating survival into valuable momentum. Meanwhile, mechanical woes sidelined trucks like Parker Eatmon's and Layne Riggs' early, emphasizing that reliability remains the primary hurdle for teams trying to establish an early-season identity.

The garage now pivots from high-speed superspeedway pack racing to the tight confines of the Streets of St. Petersburg. Road course preparation begins immediately for a field looking to build on these early baseline results.

articles.headline: Chandler Smith Dominates Atlanta in Fr8 208
articles.dek: Chandler Smith led 89 laps and held off the field through 13 cautions to win at EchoPark Speedway.
articles.body:
Chandler Smith drove his number 38 entry to victory in the Fr8 208 at EchoPark Speedway on Saturday. Starting from the pole position, Smith controlled the race by pacing the field for 89 laps of the 188-lap event. Thirteen caution periods slowed the action and bunched the field repeatedly, but Smith maintained his composure at the head of the pack to secure his second straight strong result of the young season.

Connor Zilisch charged through the field from a 26th-place start to finish second, earning the biggest upward movement of the afternoon. Timmy Hill brought his number 56 truck home in third after leading 19 laps. Dawson Sutton crossed the finish line in fourth, followed by Cole Butcher rounding out the top five. Kaden Honeycutt and Brenden Queen took sixth and seventh respectively, while Andrés Pérez de Lara finished eighth.

The race saw heavy attrition with several drivers failing to finish due to mechanical issues and accidents. Toni Breidinger and Clayton Green exited due to crashes, while Parker Eatmon and Layne Riggs dropped out with transmission failures. Jake Garcia parked his machine due to suspension trouble.

Following the event at Atlanta, Smith leads the championship standings with 88 points and one victory. Dawson Sutton sits second with 62 points, and Cole Butcher holds third with 54 points. Brenden Queen and Tyler Ankrum fill out the top five in the early season order.

articles.headline: By the Numbers: Daytona Truck Opener Sorting Out the Pack
articles.dek: A look at the statistics from the opening round of the Craftsman Truck Series season at Daytona International Speedway.
articles.body:
The Fresh From Florida 250 at Daytona International Speedway brought 35 starters to the grid for 188 laps of superspeedway competition. Attrition played a major role as the field dealt with 12 cautions throughout the afternoon.

Daniel Dye led the statistical categories by pacing the field for 68 laps from the third starting position on his way to the victory. Tyler Ankrum secured the early points lead with 35 markers after finishing second from a 22nd starting spot, leading 26 circuits along the way. Ben Rhodes followed closely in the standings with 34 points after leading 24 laps.

Luke Baldwin mounted the most significant advancement of the event. Starting 35th on the grid, Baldwin climbed 30 positions to finish fifth at the checkered flag, logging 13 laps led. Chandler Smith also factored into the front of the field by leading 21 laps and finishing fourth.

Several entries failed to complete the distance. Corey Heim and Tyler Reif exited due to accidents, Toni Breidinger retired from overheating, and Jake Garcia dropped out with a suspension issue.

Attention now shifts to EchoPark Speedway in Atlanta for the Fr8 208.

articles.headline: Daniel Dye Wins Daytona Truck Opener Amid 12 Cautions
articles.dek: Daniel Dye outlasted a chaotic superspeedway opener to win the Fresh From Florida 250 at Daytona International Speedway.
articles.body:
Daniel Dye drove the number 20 truck to victory lane in the season-opening Fresh From Florida 250 at Daytona International Speedway, taking control over 68 laps in a race slowed by 12 yellow flags. Dye secured a 1.343-second margin of victory at the finish line after surviving a race of attrition that eliminated several contenders.

Tyler Ankrum finished second after starting 22nd and leading 26 laps. Ben Rhodes brought his number 99 home in third position, leading 24 laps, while Chandler Smith took fourth after leading 21 laps. Luke Baldwin put together the biggest charge of the afternoon, advancing from 35th on the grid to finish fifth while pacing the field for 13 laps.

 Shane Van Gisbergen finished sixth, followed by Adam Andretti in seventh and Dawson Sutton in eighth. Justin Haley crossed the line ninth without leading a lap, and Frankie Muniz rounded out the top ten. Attrition played a major role in the 188-lap event, with Corey Heim and Tyler Reif sidelined by accidents, Toni Breidinger dropping out due to overheating, and Jake Garcia exiting with suspension trouble.

Tyler Ankrum leaves Daytona at the top of the championship standings with 35 points, followed closely by Ben Rhodes with 34 and Chandler Smith with 33. Because Dye and several other top finishers compete on a part-time entry basis, they do not collect championship points.

The Craftsman Truck Series continues its 25-race schedule with the second round of the season next week.

Several prominent drivers and part-time competitors enter the 2026 schedule with contracts expiring at the conclusion of the year, setting the stage for potential movement across multiple series.

Stewart Friesen enters the season in the final year of his agreement with Halmar Friesen Racing. Sources close to the team indicate that stability remains the priority for the veteran driver, who enters the year content with his current equipment package. Similarly, veteran Timmy Hill operates on an expiring deal with Hill Motorsports while balancing part-time entries and organizational growth.

Makeshift evaluations also apply to part-time competitors looking toward future opportunities in higher divisions. Drivers such as Connor Zilisch, Christopher Bell, and Ross Chastain carry expiring agreements while managing dual-series expectations. Industry chatter suggests that strong performances in the Craftsman Truck Series could influence potential promotions into the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, where seats at organizations like Richard Childress Racing or JR Motorsports could see turnover.

Team executives have maintained a quiet posture regarding future commitments while focusing entirely on the twenty-five-race schedule ahead. With the season yet to officially commence, formal negotiations remain limited to sponsor renewals and minor paint scheme finalizations for the current campaign. No definitive driver announcements for subsequent seasons are expected until the summer months provide a clearer competitive baseline.

For now, the primary objective across the pit lane involves maximizing every available stage point and race win. Expiring contracts provide an underlying narrative for veterans and rising talents alike, but the immediate pressure rests entirely on securing a strong finish in the season opener.

Spire Motorsports driver Connor Zilisch paced the field during the preseason testing session at Daytona International Speedway, laying down a lap of 49.821 seconds in the #77 machine to lead the speed charts. Teams utilized the track time to evaluate drafting tandems and run various aerodynamic setups ahead of the official season opener.

Stewart Friesen followed closely in the second position driving the #52 Halmar Friesen Racing entry. Friesen, operating in the final year of his current contract, focused heavily on race trim during the drafting simulations. Kaden Honeycutt rounded out the top three for Tricon Garage, clocking the third-fastest time in the #11 truck.

ThorSport Racing placed Cole Butcher fourth overall, while Frankie Muniz rounded out the top five in the #33 Team Reaume entry. Other notable participants in the top twenty included Tanner Gray in sixth, Adam Andretti in seventh, and Timmy Hill in eighth. Drivers utilized the multi-lane racing surface to test different lines through the high-banked turns, though several teams elected to remain in the garage during the peak heat of the afternoon.

The test session serves as the final on-track activity before technical inspection opens for the Fresh From Florida 250. Crew chiefs will review telemetry data overnight to determine gear ratios and cooling configurations for the opening race of the 2026 calendar.

Track officials reported no major incidents during the two-day test, allowing every entered organization to complete its checklist without structural damage. Qualifying for the season opener is scheduled for Friday morning, followed by the 250-mile race later that evening.

articles.headline: Tiering the Field for the 2026 Craftsman Truck Series Season
articles.dek: A comprehensive breakdown of title favorites, emerging contenders, and garage tiers as the field prepares to open the year at Daytona.
articles.body:
As the virtual Craftsman Truck Series prepares to open its 2026 campaign, the paddock settles into familiar hierarchies while new technical alliances take shape. With twenty-five races on the docket before the championship battle crystallizes, the preseason test at Daytona International Speedway provided the first tangible data points for analysts tracking winter development programs.

At the top of the board, established operations like ThorSport Racing and Tricon Garage look to dictate the pace. ThorSport brings a deep stable featuring Cole Butcher, Jake Garcia, Ben Rhodes, and Ty Majeski. Butcher flashed early speed during testing by clocking the fourth-fastest lap in the #13 machine, signaling that ThorSport's superspeedway package remains sharp. Tricon counters with a heavy-hitting lineup including Kaden Honeycutt, Tanner Gray, Adam Andretti, Nick Leitz, and Gio Ruggiero. Honeycutt established his baseline quickly at Daytona with the third-quickest time overall, positioning himself as a primary threat in the early rounds.

Moving into the dark horse category, equipment from McAnally-Hilgemann Racing and Niece Motorsports could disrupt the traditional powerhouse teams. McAnally fields Daniel Dye, Daniel Hemric, Tyler Ankrum, Christian Eckes, and Kris Wright. Their focus during the Daytona test centered on drafting lines and single-lap trim rather than pure headline speeds. Niece brings Ross Chastain, Andrés Pérez de Lara, Cleetus McFarland, and Parker Eatmon to the track. Chastain enters the year under a contract-year designation, adding organizational motivation to his part-time schedule in the #42 entry.

Spire Motorsports demands attention with a high-profile roster that features Connor Zilisch, Kyle Busch, Shane Van Gisbergen, and Connor Mosack. Zilisch dominated the timesheets in testing by topping the speed chart with the quickest lap in the #77 truck. While Daytona speeds often reflect drafting help rather than raw horsepower, pacing the test session gives Spire an immediate psychological advantage. As the circuit shifts from the drafting drills of Daytona toward intermediate tracks, these early tier divisions will face their first real competitive pressure.

interviews.quote: Job's done. We raced smart all year and brought home the trophy.
We had a fast machine right off the trailer and the crew gave me great tires all day.
We had a shot at it today. Second place hurts when you lead laps, but we will take the speed and move on.
Our thirty-eighth machine was dialed in once we got some clean air. Starting twenty-eighth is never easy here, but the guys gave me a fast truck.
Starting back in 29th makes you work for every single inch. We had enough speed to get to second, just ran out of laps.
Our truck was hooked up all day. We stayed out of trouble on the road course and capitalized when it mattered.
Thirty-fourth to seventh is a heck of a swing. We just kept our nose clean while everyone else was bouncing off the walls.
We had speed when it counted, but track position was tough to hold with all those yellows. Second is fine, but we wanted the top step.
Starting back in twenty-fifth makes you work for every single inch on a street course. The guys gave me a car that stayed out of trouble.
Good points day for us. Kept the fenders on it and brought home a podium.
We started too far back but fought all day to get that runner-up spot.
Our truck was hooked up all day. Just needed to hit our marks on the restarts.
Good points day to start the year. We wanted the win, but second is solid.
Starting dead last gives you plenty of work to do. We found a way through the mess.
Our truck was hooked up all night. Just had to survive the chaos at the end.

notes.bryan dauzat: Dauzat falls short of the playoff threshold despite solid intermediate speed through twenty five events.

notes.chandler smith: Smith closed out his campaign showcasing incredible speed by charging from twenty eighth to win cleanly.
notes.cole butcher: Butcher left everyone stunned by marching from thirty second to victory lane at the ECOSAVE 200.

season.headline: Looking back
